successCriteria.description: A successful login returns an object with a `token` (minted via signToken for the employee's id+role) and a `profile` that is an EmployeeProfile containing no `passwordHash` and no `terminationDate`.
Wrong email and wrong password produce the SAME error — a single UnauthorizedError('Invalid email or password') — so the two failure modes are indistinguishable (no account enumeration).
The login endpoint is reachable WITHOUT a bearer token (its path is in the public-path set) and returns 200 with `{ token, profile }` on valid credentials.
A request body whose `email` or `password` is not a string is rejected with a ValidationError (400), not a 500.
The auth module's public entry point re-exports IAuthService, AuthService, and authRoutes, and the app registers authRoutes so the endpoint is mounted at runtime.

constraints: Use only the already-installed bcrypt (^5.0.1) and jsonwebtoken (^8.5.1) with their existing @types packages; add no new libraries.
No controller file — the route handler calls the auth service directly, matching the codebase's universal routes-call-services shape.
The auth service must not import the employee module's module-local toEmployeeProfile helper; it defines its own EmployeeProfile mapper that omits passwordHash and terminationDate.
Login is a read-only credential check plus a non-persistent token mint — no transaction, no IUnitOfWork, no audit record, no repository access in the auth module.
Never log the password, the token, or the passwordHash (GP-004); the route's error logging must not emit credentials.
outOfScope: No token refresh, logout, registration, or password reset — only the single login operation.
No OIDC/corporate identity integration — local bcrypt credential check only.
No audit-log write for login (GP-002 does not apply to a non-persistent credential check).
No GET /employees/me or other authenticated read endpoints — those are later phases.

entityInvariants.invariant: The token minted at login carries sub = employee.id and role = employee.role (the AuthUser contract), and is produced by the existing signToken — its payload shape must not change.
The profile returned from login is the shared EmployeeProfile shape and must never contain passwordHash or terminationDate.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Public — no authentication required; the endpoint is exempted from the auth preHandler via the public-path set.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Missing employee and failed password compare both throw the SAME UnauthorizedError('Invalid email or password'); non-string email/password rejected with ValidationError.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Reuse signToken (not a local jwt.sign) to mint the token, passing { id, role } matching the AuthUser shape.
Reuse the resolveActor/sendError error-mapping shape (AppError -> { error, code } with correct status, else 500) so error mapping stays identical across modules.
The returned profile must match the shared EmployeeProfile type (imported from shared/types), not a locally re-declared shape.
Use the existing UnauthorizedError and ValidationError classes (not new error types) so the { error, code } contract and status codes stay consistent.
Call IEmployeeService.getEmployeeByEmail (which throws NotFoundError on unknown email) and convert that NotFoundError to the same UnauthorizedError as a failed compare.

integrationPoints.why: Resolves the caller by email and supplies the passwordHash to compare; its NotFoundError must be mapped to UnauthorizedError.
Mints the JWT and exempts the login path from the auth preHandler.
The profile return type and the role carried in the token payload.
authRoutes must be registered after registerAuth so the public-path exemption applies and the endpoint is mounted.
